target.title: fix: escape assistant-authored transcript role headers
target.body:
Related: #99253

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where assistant-authored text could visually resemble a fresh transcript/user turn when the model emits role-header-shaped lines such as `user[...]`, `[timestamp] user:`, or `<User ...>` inside an assistant reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused assistant-output boundary for transcript-role-looking headers:

- Assistant visible text now escapes supported role-header-looking line prefixes outside Markdown code regions.
- Chat display history applies the same escaping only to assistant-authored display text, leaving real user text and tool payloads unchanged.
- Message-end diagnostics now warn when assistant text contains a transcript-role-looking header, without logging the original assistant text into warning metadata.

This does not change structured tool dispatch. The change keeps assistant-authored role-looking text inert and visually distinct while preserving legitimate code examples and tool payloads.

## User Impact

Users and operators can distinguish real session turns from assistant-authored transcript-looking text more reliably. Suspicious assistant completions also leave a diagnostic signal that can be investigated without exposing the generated text in warning metadata.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD` passed after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`.
- Duplicate check found no existing open PR for issue `#99253` or branch `snowzlmbot:fix/issue-99253-assistant-role-header` before opening this PR.

- `Workflow Sanity / no-tabs`: passed.

Risk:

- The detector is intentionally line-start scoped and skips Markdown code regions to reduce false positives in quoted transcript examples.
- This PR covers display escaping and diagnostics. It does not add a new fail-closed same-turn tool execution policy.
